A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same attention-rank and Active Subspace Initialization study despite the changed title. All 22 pages of v2 and 27 pages of v3, including figures, equations and appendices, support comparison. Changed metrics and experimental settings can be identified separately.

before.justification: Sections 4–5 and the appendices report original activation-spectrum analyses, SAE and Lorsa training results, scaling experiments and ablations.

after.justification: The paper retains original empirical results and adds SVD stability measurements, further SAE evaluations, statistical tests and blinded feature-quality assessments.

M1.justification: The ASI and SparseAdam framework remains, but the initialization routines change. Appendix I in v2 initializes SAE weights using random subspace coefficients; Appendix K in v3 instead projects the full decoder matrix through V_active V_active^T. Lorsa switches from output-side SVD and decoder-to-encoder tying to input/value-side SVD and encoder-to-decoder tying. These are procedural refinements within the existing approach.

E1.justification: Appendix I.2 adds actual ASI evaluation on fineweb-edu, and Appendix N introduces blinded semantic-consistency evaluation beyond reconstruction and dead-feature measurement. Existing general-text, code, scientific-text and Chinese coverage remains. Github and Arxiv already appear in v2; the clarified SlimPajama subset names do not establish new coverage.

E2.justification: The Lorsa comparison expands from Base versus ASI in v2 Figure 8 to TopK, AuxK and ASI in v3 Figure 9, adding AuxK within that experiment. The principal SAE/scaling comparators, random-subspace baseline and JumpReLU Pre-Act Loss comparator were already evaluated in v2.

E3.justification: The principal dimensionality metric changes from a 99%-variance threshold to entropy-based effective rank. Outside scaling, stated SAE defaults change from batch size 32768 and Adam learning rate 2e-4 to 4096 and 4e-5. The earlier 2.5B-token scaling budget becomes an 800M-token general specification. Lorsa's layer sweep becomes a middle-layer sparsity sweep, and additional model/site configurations and blinded feature scoring are introduced. These reported changes do not establish which retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v3 adds SVD sample-stability analysis, dictionary-size/sparsity controls for the rank–dead-feature relationship, broader ASI robustness evaluations, and monosemanticity/dead-subspace analyses in Appendices C, F, I and N. Random-subspace, near-full-rank and high-initial-sparsity ablations are retained under new appendix labels. The variance-threshold sensitivity sweep in v2 Appendix F is removed.

E5.justification: v3 newly reports three-seed means and standard deviations for Figures 6–7 and Table 4, 15 independent seeded trials with one-sided Welch tests in Appendix H, and five SVD samples with coefficients of variation in Appendix C. v2 does not provide these uncertainty procedures or corresponding run counts, so an increase over known v2 repetition counts cannot be inferred.

E6.justification: v3 replaces dimensionality estimates and revises SAE/Lorsa result displays while adding extensive numerical results in Tables 1–10. For example, the new Qwen3-8B/fineweb-edu layer-8 comparison reports normalized MSE of 0.31228 for Base, 0.28849 for AuxK and 0.28533 for ASI. Table 10 adds dead-subspace MSE of 0.00350 versus 0.00334. The headline 87%-to-below-1% result remains; changed metrics and budgets limit direct cross-version performance comparisons.

T1.justification: Section 4.1 replaces the variance-threshold dimension definition with Definition 4.1, effective rank computed from the entropy of normalized singular values. The attention variance factorization and head-subspace bound remain substantively unchanged. Appendix B states the formula for the existing loss-recovery metric; no new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain low-rank attention outputs, their association with dead features, and ASI with SparseAdam. However, the abstract's quantitative claim changes from roughly 60% of directions capturing 99% of variance to roughly 60% effective rank. It also qualifies the output projection's role from inducing the phenomenon to strongly shaping it.

C2.justification: v3 substantially extends interpretation: Appendix N argues that feature quality and dead-subspace reconstruction are preserved and proposes weak signal or absent standalone features as explanations for dead-subspace behavior. Section 6 suggests architectural changes to mitigate rank collapse, while Appendix I links remaining dead features to fixed-subspace-dimension mismatch. Existing qualifications concerning unresolved causality and high-initial-L0 failure remain.

D1.justification: New Appendix O supplies a detailed Lorsa recipe, including head/QK-group dimensions, optimizer settings, learning-rate schedule, 2048-token sequences, training budget and initialization distributions. SAE settings and pseudocode are also revised, and dataset-component selection is clarified. Some ambiguity remains because ASI-specific Q/K copying in Section 5.4 is not clearly distinguished from the general Xavier initialization described in Appendix O.2.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds representation-collapse literature, including Hua, Tian and Jing, and reframes the linear-representation discussion around superposition while qualifying claims of empirical validation with Sharkey et al. New references support effective rank and feature evaluation, while Guth et al. is removed. The core positioning relative to attention-pattern approximation, compression and single-head rank bottlenecks remains.

P1.justification: The paper is retitled, dimensionality terminology is revised throughout, and substantial related-work, quantification, initialization and discussion passages are rewritten. Experimental settings receive a separate subsection, and existing appendices are extensively reordered around the new analyses. Author contributions are added and the earlier LLM-use declaration is removed.

P2.justification: The main text and references change from single-column to two-column layout. Most plots are redrawn or rearranged, the introductory illustration is relocated and numbered, the rank–dead-feature display gains a scatter panel, and ten tables are introduced. These changes substantially alter the visual presentation beyond figure renumbering and numerical updates.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially strengthens evidence that was limited in v2: repeated-seed estimates and significance tests establish reliability, additional layers and Qwen3/fineweb-edu evaluations test ASI's generality, and feature-quality/dead-subspace checks address whether reducing dead features sacrifices useful representations. These additions materially support the practical contribution. Changed metrics and budgets complicate cross-version score comparisons, and Lorsa initialization remains partly ambiguous, but those limitations do not outweigh the substantial gains in empirical support.
